chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, who said:

I saw Al-Rida (peace be upon him) bid farewell to the House. When he wanted to leave the door of the mosque, he fell into prostration. Then he stood up, faced the Ka'bah, and said: 'O God, I return upon the belief that there is no god but God.'

key_terms.أَنْقَلِبُ: I return (indicating a return to a state or condition)
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (a title for Imam Ali al-Rida, the 8th Shia Imam)
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House (referring to the Ka'bah in Mecca)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Ka'bah (the cubic structure in Mecca towards which Muslims face in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Rida do when leaving the mosque to bid farewell to the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this narration highlights Imam Al-Rida’s (AS) personal devotion and the ritual of *tawaf* or farewell prostration at the Ka'bah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imams as perfect exemplars of worship. The supplication 'Allahumma inni anqalib ala an la ilaha illa Allah' (O God, I return to the belief that there is no god but God) underscores the concept of *tawhid* as both a foundational creed and a continuous spiritual state, resonating with the Shia scholarly view of the Imam as the living proof of God on earth.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 30-43 Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Waleed - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on theauthority of Ibrahim ibn Hashem, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, “

I saw Al-Ridha (s) say farewell to the House (of God). When he wanted to leave the mosque door, he (s) fell into prostration. Then he stood up, faced the Qibla - direction of prayer - and said, ‘O my God! I will return with the belief that there is no god but Thee.’”
